exposure: Neonates with normal birth weight and no other complications such as hyperbirilubinemia, hypoglycemia or bacterial infections
Elective Cesarean section at 37 weeks gestation
Elective Cesarean section at 38 weeks gestation
Gestational age at birth (37 weeks vs 38 weeks)
cohort: Newborns delivered by elective Cesarean section at 37 or 38 weeks gestation between 2006 and 2012 at a single hospital in Japan (n = 684)
finding: Newborns delivered via elective Cesarean section at 37 weeks gestation had a significantly higher incidence of neonatal complications, particularly adverse respiratory outcomes, compared to those delivered at 38 weeks.
mod_finding: Elective Cesarean section at 37 weeks gestation was associated with increased neonatal complications compared to 38 weeks.
